passage:
Subject: Thank you for Tuesday

Dear Pallavi,

Thank you for meeting me at the coffee counter. I came with three questions written on a card, and your answers were clear. First, skills: you said to get comfortable with spreadsheets and with writing short, clear updates. Second, entry paths: an internship in third year, or a junior analyst opening through campus placements. Third, daily work: mostly cleaning data in the mornings and meetings after lunch. I took notes on all of it, and next week I will compare them with what a second alumnus tells me. I have already signed up for a spreadsheet course. Thank you again for your time.

Best wishes,
Lokesh

qa.q: What were the three questions about?
qa.a: The three questions were about skills, entry paths and daily work.

qa.q: How might Lokesh have felt going into the meeting with a card of written questions?
qa.a: Lokesh probably felt keen but a little nervous, wanting to make good use of the time and get a clear picture for planning.

qa.q: What could Lokesh do with the notes next?
qa.a: Lokesh could compare them with the second alumnus's answers, see what matches, and choose a first step.

qa.q: How might Pallavi have felt on receiving a student with prepared questions?
qa.a: Pallavi may have felt pleased and respected, since the student took time to prepare.
